## Signal Flow (Reverb Window)

Live Input > Input Gain > AA Filter > Pitch Counter decimation > ADPCM Encode > ADPCM Decode > Gauss Interpolation > Reverb Core

- AA Filter and Gauss are toggleable. ADPCM path is always-on (no toggle).
- Input Rate (pitch register) drives three stages: AA cutoff, decimation rate, and Gauss interpolation index.
- Sampler voice mixer output goes DIRECTLY to reverb send — does NOT pass through the ADPCM path again. Authentic to PS1.

## Missing PS1 SPU Sampler Features

### High Priority (v1.9 candidates, already in deferred list)
1. PMON (Pitch Modulation) — voice N output modulates voice N+1 pitch. Vibrato, FM synthesis.
2. NON (Noise Generator) — LFSR noise replaces ADPCM output for a voice. Hi-hats, cymbals, wind.
3. Volume Sweep — automatic per-voice volume ramp (linear/exponential). Tremolo, fades.
4. Signed Volume / Phase Inversion — negative volume values flip phase. Stereo widening, cancellation.

### Lower Priority (completeness)
5. ENDX (Voice Status) — flags showing which voices hit loop-end. CPU polls for one-shot completion.
6. SPU IRQ — interrupt on voice reading specific RAM address. Music sync trigger.
7. CD/External Input Mixing — stereo line-in with own volume, mixes at master output, optional reverb send.
8. Master Volume Sweep — global L/R volume registers support hardware-driven sweep.

## PS1 Audio Paths (Reference)

### Path 1: SPU RAM (what we've built)
- Samples in 512 KB buffer. 24 voices with pitch, ADSR, reverb.
- Instant trigger, full real-time control.
- ~15-20 sec total audio at 22050 Hz if entire buffer used.

### Path 2: CD-DA (Red Book Audio)
- Standard audio CD tracks on game disc. CD drive's own DAC plays independently.
- Zero RAM cost, perfect CD quality. Early PS1 games (Ridge Racer, WipEout).
- Downside: disc space, seek gaps on loop, music skips if drive busy loading.

### Path 3: CD-XA (Streaming ADPCM)
- Interleaved compressed audio woven between game data sectors on disc.
- Different codec than SPU ADPCM — own block format, decoded by CD drive DSP in hardware.
- Decoded audio routes into SPU's CD input, mixes with 24 voices, can feed reverb.
- Stereo 37.8 kHz or mono 18.9 kHz. 8 interleave channels for multiplexing.
- Zero SPU RAM consumed. Minutes of continuous audio.
- No pitch/envelope control (it's a stream, not a sample).
- 100-300ms seek to start new stream. Only one XA stream at a time.

### How Studios Split It
- Music: XA streaming (long, no RAM cost) — FF7, MGS, most later PS1 titles
- SFX: SPU RAM (instant, pitch control, short) — universal
- Dialogue: XA streaming (long, sequential) — MGS codec, FF7 battle quotes
- FMV: XA audio interleaved with MDEC video — all PS1 cutscenes
- Exception: Crash Bandicoot — Naughty Dog fit everything in SPU RAM
